html:
The Wangaaypuwan, also known as the Wongaibon, are an Aboriginal Australian people of western New South Wales, between today's Nyngan, the Bogan River and west toward Ivanhoe. They are one branch of the Ngiyampaa nation.

Their neighbours were the Wailwan to the northeast, the Barranbinya and Gunu to the north and the Paaruntyi beyond. In 1835 the botanist Richard Cunningham strayed from Thomas Mitchell's expedition on the Bogan River and was killed by local people. Sheep runs reached the Bogan in the late 1830s and 1840s.
